summary: The reader has an undergraduate computer science education at introductory depth: discrete mathematics (integers, divisibility, modular arithmetic, gcd and primes, binomial coefficients, induction, the field of two elements with XOR), algorithms (the big-O family, divide-and-conquer recurrences, the RAM and multitape Turing models), calculus (limits, convergence of sequences and series, geometric series, basic integrals), elementary linear algebra over the reals and F_2 (vector spaces, linear maps, rank, dot products, matrix products), and complex numbers with modulus and polar form. The reader has not reached specialist algebra, tensor products, bilinear forms, eigen-theory beyond the basics, analysis (liminf and limsup), or numerical analysis, so the main theorem's proof and its network and transform machinery must be explained.

known.name: Logarithms and exponentials
known.gloss: The logarithm log_b x is the exponent to which the base b must be raised to give x, and exp is its inverse, so that log(xy) = log x + log y and b^(log_b x) = x.

known.name: Floor and ceiling functions
known.gloss: The floor of x is the largest integer not exceeding x, and the ceiling of x is the smallest integer not less than x.

known.name: Positional (radix) representation
known.gloss: A nonnegative integer written in base b is a finite string of digits, each between 0 and b-1, whose value is the sum of each digit times the corresponding power of b.

known.name: Field of two elements
known.gloss: The field F_2 has the two elements 0 and 1, with addition given by XOR and multiplication given by AND.

known.name: Bitwise XOR
known.gloss: XOR of two bits is 1 exactly when the bits differ, and bitwise XOR of two equal-length bit strings applies this to each position.

known.name: Modular arithmetic and congruences
known.gloss: Two integers are congruent modulo m when they differ by a multiple of m, and addition and multiplication of residue classes modulo m are well defined by working with representatives.

known.name: Greatest common divisor and the Euclidean algorithm
known.gloss: The gcd of two integers is the largest integer dividing both, two integers are coprime when their gcd is 1, and the Euclidean algorithm computes the gcd by repeated division with remainder.

known.name: Prime numbers
known.gloss: A prime is an integer greater than 1 whose only positive divisors are 1 and itself, and every integer greater than 1 factors uniquely into primes.

known.name: Binomial coefficients and counting subsets
known.gloss: The binomial coefficient binom(n,k) counts the k-element subsets of an n-element set and equals n!/(k!(n-k)!).

known.name: Mathematical induction
aliases: recursion on the number of ranges
known.gloss: Induction proves a statement for all natural numbers by proving a base case and showing that the statement for n+1 follows from the statement for n, or from all smaller values in strong induction.

known.name: Divide-and-conquer recurrence
known.gloss: A divide-and-conquer recurrence expresses the cost on an input of size n in terms of the costs on smaller subproblems plus the cost of combining them, and its solution is found by unrolling the recursion.

known.name: Random-access machine model
known.gloss: The random-access machine has a finite program and memory cells addressed by integers, so that any cell can be read or written in one step.

known.name: Limits and convergence of sequences
aliases: limit as n tends to infinity
known.gloss: A sequence converges to L when its terms eventually stay arbitrarily close to L, and the limit of a ratio is the ratio of the limits when both converge.

known.name: Convergence of series
known.gloss: An infinite series converges when its sequence of partial sums converges, and its sum is the limit of those partial sums.

known.name: Geometric series
aliases: sum of powers of a ratio
known.gloss: A geometric series is a sum of the form a + ar + ar^2 + ... + ar^k, which equals a(1 - r^(k+1))/(1 - r) for r not equal to 1 and is bounded by a/(1 - r) when |r| < 1.

known.name: Big-Omega, big-Theta and little-o notation
known.gloss: Omega(f) bounds a function below by a constant multiple of f for large inputs, Theta(f) bounds it both above and below, and o(f) means the ratio to f tends to zero.

known.name: Dot product and orthogonal vectors
known.gloss: The dot product of two vectors of the same length is the sum of the products of their corresponding entries, and two vectors are orthogonal when this sum is zero.

known.name: Matrix product, transpose, and special matrices
known.gloss: The product of an m-by-k and a k-by-n matrix is the m-by-n matrix of dot products of rows and columns, the transpose swaps rows and columns, and a diagonal, triangular, or permutation matrix has the stated zero pattern.

known.name: Complex modulus, conjugate and polar form
aliases: absolute value of a complex number
known.gloss: The modulus |a+bi| of a complex number is sqrt(a^2+b^2), its conjugate is a-bi, and every nonzero complex number can be written as r e^(i theta) with r > 0 and a real angle theta.

known.name: Fixed-point arithmetic
known.gloss: A fixed-point number is an integer scaled by a fixed power of two, so that arithmetic on such numbers is integer arithmetic with a fixed binary point.
